purpose: Prevent a user-identity or operator-lifecycle action from becoming accidental authority to delete another person's Brain.

relationship_inventory.rule: No safe result may be produced from a partial or unverified workspace relationship inventory.

invariants: erase_subject_brain is emitted only where workspace.subject_id exactly equals the subject-erasure identity
operator access is revoked for differently-subjected workspaces the removed person owns or operates
ownership of a differently-subjected Brain creates a transfer-or-customer-closure gate
operator removal for a person who is also a Brain subject preserves that Brain behind a separate subject decision
auth-user deletion remains false while any protected Brain needs custody action
duplicate or unverified relationship evidence fails closed
verified_scenarios: owner removal for a different subject
one person's own Brain plus customer Brains they operate
operator removal where the operator is also the Brain subject

execution_boundary.reason: The current schema still uses cascading auth-user owner references. A later non-cascading custody design and multi-identity database canary must prove the policy before execution.

next_gate: Bind all four R18 owner paths to this relationship-aware custody policy, then design and verify a non-cascading owner-reference candidate without changing a linked database.
